claims.text: A City of Dallas briefing to the council's Finance Committee set out a plan to put 100 AI enabled cameras on Sanitation brush trucks.

claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology, Finance Committee briefing (15 pages)

claims.text: The briefing describes the hardware as 2 cameras mounted on 1 city vehicle.

claims.publisher: City of Dallas, Code Compliance and Sanitation

claims.text: The briefing lists the property conditions the software detects as bulk trash participation, collapsing structures, trash, tires, illegal dumping, graffiti, boarded windows or doors and high grass.

claims.document: Update on the Use of AI-Powered Camera Technology, Finance Committee briefing (15 pages)
claims.publisher: City of Dallas, Code Compliance and Sanitation

claims.text: The briefing describes a three-year contract for an estimated $2,556,000, subject to annual City Council appropriations.

claims.publisher: City of Dallas, Code Compliance and Sanitation

claims.publisher: City of Dallas, Code Compliance and Sanitation

claims.text: The city may terminate the contract at any time with 10 days' written notice and without penalty.

claims.publisher: City of Dallas, Code Compliance and Sanitation

claims.text: The briefing states the system is neither a staff replacement nor automated ticketing.

claims.publisher: City of Dallas, Code Compliance and Sanitation

claims.text: A City of Dallas memo dated September 8th, 2026 detailed the findings and costs of the AI powered cameras the city has used on its trash trucks since early 2026.
claims.quote: A September 8 memo from the City of Dallas detailed the findings and costs of AI-powered cameras that the city has been using on its trash trucks since early 2026.
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: According to the memo the cameras have scanned 10,000 properties and found 3,700 violations that resulted in notices from the city.
claims.quote: According to the memo, the cameras have scanned 10,000 properties and have resulted in 3,700 violations, resulting in notices from the city.
claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: The memo counts 57 citations at 34 properties and states citations are issued only after a code officer inspects the property in person and notifies the owner.

claims.document: AI-powered cameras on Dallas trash trucks result in almost 4,000 notices, 57 citations

claims.text: The cameras are made by City Detect and scan homes and buildings for potential code violations.

claims.text: The system flags potential code violations and generates blight scores that help Code Compliance decide which properties to review first.

rejected.finding: A funnel or rate running from 10,000 properties scanned to 3,700 courtesy notices, 300 cases and 57 citations
rejected.reason: The memo's counts measure different things and no source presents them as a step by step count. No funnel, rate or ratio between them is drawn or printed. Only the memo's own 68 percent (c55) is carried.

rejected.finding: A count of cameras per truck or of trucks
rejected.reason: The city's briefing plans 100 cameras and describes 2 cameras on 1 city vehicle. No source carried here counts the trucks, so no frame counts cameras on a truck.
A rounded headline figure. The body's 3,700 (c46) and Dallas Express's approximately 3,700 property owners (c53) are carried instead.
The sentence could not be read word for word past its opening, so the 70 percent figure is not carried. The memo's 39 citations, 68 percent, is carried instead from Dallas Express (c55).
